mainTopic: How the משנה counts its list of כריתות: mistakes in עבודה זרה, general categories, אוב and ידעוני, and what counts as an action
overview: The amud opens by looking for a case of שגגת עבודה זרה וזדון עבודות. The גמרא gives three ways to picture it: someone who thinks idol worship is allowed, a תינוק שנשבה, or an adult who thinks only silver and gold idols are forbidden. רב ביבי then explains that the משנה's list of כריתות names general categories like שבת and עבודה זרה. The גמרא shows why his own question about 'thirty-seven' is still fair. רבי ירמיה asks about two punishments under one לאו, and רבי זירא points to אוב and ידעוני. רבי יוחנן says ידעוני is left off the כרת list because it shares one לאו with אוב. ריש לקיש says it is left off because it has no action. This leads to a discussion of what counts as an action for רבי עקיבא and for the רבנן, and why the משנה excludes only the מגדף. The amud ends with עולא, רבא and אביי defining the בעל אוב and the חובר חבר, and with a new challenge from רבי יוחנן's view that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is someone who thinks idol worship is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The mistake in עבודה זרה is a person who says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier ideas for how to picture a mistake about עבודה זרה did not work. Now the גמרא offers a new case: the person simply believes idol worship is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His mistake comes from not knowing the law, not from forgetting. He does not know that עבודה זרה is forbidden. But he does know that bowing, sacrificing and the other acts of worship are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who says (thinks) it is permitted. His mistake comes from not knowing the law.
An accidental or mistaken sin.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he says it is permitted,
phrases.notes: He means the person believes idol worship itself is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new case after earlier attempts (on the previous amud) were turned down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could not find a workable case of a mistake about עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone who thinks עבודה זרה is permitted counts as having made a mistake about עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Proof from רבא's question to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: When רבא asked רב נחמן about שבת, he only asked how many offerings such a person brings. He never asked whether the person is free of any offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא asked רב נחמן only whether such a person is liable for one offering or for two. He did not ask whether he is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last step. It points to a known question about שבת where the person did not know the basic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asked about someone who did not know about שבת and did not know about the forbidden מלאכות. He only wondered whether this person brings one חטאת or two. Nobody imagined he would be free of any חטאת. So not knowing the law counts as a real שגגה, and the same is true for עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: He only asked up to this point and no further.
He is liable.
To be completely exempt.

phrases.english: For he did not ask of him any further
phrases.notes: This points to a question about someone who knew neither about שבת nor about its מלאכות.

phrases.english: (that is, רבא of רב נחמן)
than whether he is liable for one
or whether he is liable for two,
but about being exempt completely
he did not ask him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּעַד כָּאן לָא קָבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That 'saying it is permitted' counts as a שגגה that requires a חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's question to רב נחמן about someone who knew neither שבת nor its מלאכות.

steps.title: רב פפא: a child captured among non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: A תינוק שנשבה knows that idol worship in general is forbidden. He does not know that these particular idols are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: You can find this case with a child captured among the non-Jews. He knows idol worship is forbidden, but he does not know that these particular idols are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different way to picture a mistake about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This child grew up without learning Torah. He has a general idea that עבודה זרה is wrong. But he does not realize that the objects in front of him count as עבודה זרה. That is his mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find this case.
A child taken captive and raised among non-Jews.

phrases.english: רב פפא said: You find it
in a child who was captured among the gentiles,
who knows that idol worship is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לָא יָדַע דַּאֲסִירָן.
phrases.english: but these idols he does not know are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different case.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knows the general rule but not that it covers these idols.

steps.title: An adult who misreads the פסוק about silver and gold gods
steps.stepSummary: Even an adult can make this mistake. He thinks only silver and gold idols are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say it is even about an adult who misunderstood the פסוק 'Do not make with Me gods of silver and gods of gold.' He thinks bowing is forbidden only to silver and gold idols, and idols of other materials are allowed. That is a mistake about עבודה זרה while knowing the acts of worship are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer. It shows the case does not have to be about a captured child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The adult read the פסוק too narrowly. He thinks it only forbids gods of silver and gold. So when he bows to a wooden or stone idol, he does not know it is עבודה זרה, even though he knows bowing to an idol is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: a way of bringing another answer.
He made a mistake in this פסוק.
Bowing down.
A mistake about idol worship while knowing the acts of worship are forbidden.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to picture this case: (1) he thinks עבודה זרה is permitted; (2) a תינוק שנשבה; (3) an adult who thinks only silver and gold idols are forbidden.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
you may even say it is about an adult –
for example, where he erred in this verse:
"You shall not make with Me
phrases.notes: שמות 20:20

phrases.english: gods of silver and gods of gold, etc."
He thinks: when bowing is forbidden,
it is to an idol of silver and gold,
but one of other materials is permitted,
and that is unwitting about idol worship
and intentional about the acts of worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּגָדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב פפא's idea so it also covers an adult.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only a captured child could make this kind of mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: An adult who misreads the פסוק can make it too.

steps.title: The משנה counts only general categories
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, quoting רב ביבי, says the משנה lists the general names, like שבת and עבודה זרה. It does not count each separate offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said in the name of רב ביבי: The תנא lists the general category of שבת and the general category of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a completely new approach to the משנה's list. It does not need to find a case where someone brings several offerings for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers tried to explain why the list counts in a way that leads to many offerings. Here the list is read as naming general categories only. It is not a careful count of how many offerings a person brings.

keyTerms.meaning: A name, meaning a general category.

phrases.english: רב אחא, son of רב איקא,
said in the name of רב ביבי:
The תנא teaches the category of שבת
and the category of idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיבִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves behind the search for cases and reads the משנה's list differently.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list names categories. It does not count each separate offering.

steps.title: How do we know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the משנה lists only categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. It gets us ready for the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא's reading is a claim about how the משנה is written. So the גמרא asks for evidence from the wording of the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the משנה counts only general categories.

steps.title: Proof: בתו מאנוסתו is not listed separately
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists 'a woman and her daughter' and 'a married woman.' It does not list 'his daughter from a woman he violated.' So it must be listing general categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה teaches: 'One who has relations with a woman and her daughter, and with a married woman.' But there is also his daughter from a woman he violated, and the משנה does not list it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב אחא's point from a missing case in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בתו מאנוסתו is a separate כרת sin, yet the משנה never mentions it by name. That only makes sense if it is included inside the general category 'a woman and her daughter.' So the משנה gives categories, not a full detailed count.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman and her daughter: a forbidden relationship.
A married woman.
His daughter from a woman he violated.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בתו מאנוסתו is allowed because the משנה leaves it out. It is forbidden. It is simply included inside the general category of 'a woman and her daughter.'

phrases.english: From that it teaches: one who has relations with a woman and her daughter
and with a married woman,
but there is his daughter from his violated woman,
phrases.notes: Since he never married her mother, the Torah does not name this case directly, but it is still a כרת sin.

phrases.english: which it does not teach!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָתָנֵי: הַבָּא עַל אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה lists general categories.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה leaves out בתו מאנוסתו and lets it be included under 'a woman and her daughter.'

steps.title: Maybe the משנה only lists sins written openly in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The Sages push back on the proof. Maybe the משנה leaves out 'his daughter from a woman he violated' only because that case is not written openly in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: the משנה teaches the cases that are written in the תורה. It does not teach the cases that are not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason why the משנה might leave out 'his daughter from a woman he violated.' This weakens the proof from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said: the משנה leaves out that case, so it must be listing only categories. Here the גמרא offers a different reason. That case is learned through a דרשה and is not written openly, and the משנה only counts sins that are written openly. If that is true, the proof for 'categories only' falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: the ones that are written openly in the תורה
he (the תנא of the משנה) teaches or lists

phrases.english: They say: he teaches the ones that are written;
phrases.notes: 'Written' means stated openly in a פסוק, not learned through a דרשה.

phrases.english: the ones that are not written, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: דִּכְתִיבָן קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7 by giving another reason the case is left out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the missing case of 'his daughter from a woman he violated'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case may be missing only because it is learned through a דרשה, not because the משנה lists general categories.

steps.title: But some written cases are also missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the pushback. בת אשתו, בת בתה and בת בנה are written openly in the תורה, and the משנה still does not list them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the cases of his wife's daughter, her daughter's daughter, and her son's daughter. They are written in the תורה, and the משנה does not teach them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the idea 'the משנה lists only written cases' does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה listed every written case, these three should appear on their own. They do not. So 'written vs. not written' cannot explain what the משנה leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: his wife's daughter
his wife's daughter's daughter
his wife's son's daughter

phrases.english: But there is his wife's daughter,
and her daughter's daughter, and her son's daughter,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17

phrases.english: which are written, and he does not teach them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא בַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבַת בִּתָּהּ וּבַת בְּנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the pushback in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that the משנה lists every case written openly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some cases written openly are also missing from the משנה, so 'written vs. not written' cannot be the rule.

steps.title: The משנה lists categories, so שבת and עבודה זרה are categories too
steps.stepSummary: Since those written cases are missing, the משנה must list the general category 'אשה ובתה'. In the same way it lists the categories of שבת and עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he teaches the category of 'a woman and her daughter.' So too, he teaches the category of שבת and the category of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה lists general categories. This brings back רב ביבי's answer from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heading 'אשה ובתה' covers all the related cases, written or learned. So the משנה is clearly listing headings, not every single sin. The same is true for שבת and עבודה זרה, which fully supports step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: a name or heading; a general category
a woman and her daughter; the משנה's heading for this group of עריות

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of the 36 כריתות lists general headings (שֵׁם), not every separate sin. 'אשה ובתה' covers several cases, and 'שבת' and 'עבודה זרה' each count once.

phrases.english: Rather, he teaches the category of 'a woman and her daughter'?
phrases.notes: This is said as 'you must admit it' — the only way to explain the missing cases.

phrases.english: So too: the category of שבת
and the category of עבודה זרה he teaches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: שֵׁם אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 9 and brings the proof of step 7 back to life.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה lists general categories, so each of שבת and עבודה זרה counts once.

steps.title: רב אחא shows a contradiction in רב ביבי's words
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא asks: did רב ביבי בר אביי really say the משנה lists categories? There is a ruling that offering up limbs outside makes a person liable in two separate ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב איקא, set one statement of רב ביבי against another. Did רב ביבי בר אביי really say the משנה teaches the category of שבת and the category of עבודה זרה? But it was taught: one who offers up limbs from inside outside is liable, and limbs from outside outside is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רב אחא sets up a contradiction between two statements of רב ביבי, starting with a ruling about offering up limbs outside the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling lists two separate liabilities. One is for limbs of an animal slaughtered inside the Temple and offered outside. The other is for an animal slaughtered outside and offered outside. This step only sets up the case. The next step shows how רב ביבי reacted to it.

keyTerms.meaning: he set one statement of his against another statement of his
limbs of an offering slaughtered inside the Temple
outside the Temple
liable (here, to bring a קרבן חטאת)

phrases.english: Rav Aha, son of Rav Ika,
set his own statement against his own statement:
phrases.notes: 'His' means רב ביבי בר אביי. Two of his own statements seem to clash.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי,
phrases.english: Did Rav Beivai bar Abaye say this,
that he teaches the category of Shabbat
and teaches the category of idol worship?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאִיתְּמַר: הַמַּעֲלֶה אֵבְרֵי פְּנִים בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: But it was stated: One who offers up limbs from inside, outside, is liable;
phrases.notes: The animal was slaughtered properly in the Temple, but its limbs were burned on an altar outside.

phrases.english: limbs from outside, outside, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא רָמֵי דִּילֵיהּ אַדִּילֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'categories' answer is settled, it is questioned through another statement of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether רב ביבי בר אביי really held that the משנה lists only categories.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a second statement of רב ביבי, about two kinds of offering up outside, that will seem to clash with his 'categories' answer.

steps.title: Why did רב ביבי ask about 37? He could just say 'the category of offering up'
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי once asked: if both kinds of offering up make a person liable, there should be 37 כריתות, not 36. רב אחא asks: why was that hard for him? By his own rule, the משנה lists the one category of 'offering up'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ביבי בר אביי found it difficult: 'If so, what we learned — there are 36 כריתות in the תורה — they are really 37, because there is offering up and offering up!' What is difficult for him? Let him answer: the משנה teaches the category of offering up!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא finishes the contradiction. רב ביבי's own question shows he thought the משנה counts every sin. That clashes with his answer that the משנה lists categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To ask 'it should be 37,' רב ביבי must have thought each kind of offering up counts on its own. But in step 5 he said the משנה lists headings. If so, both kinds fit under one heading, 'offering up,' and his question would never start.

keyTerms.meaning: sins that carry the punishment of כרת
offering up a קרבן on an altar
let him answer
if so

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not saying there are 37 כריתות. He is showing that רב ביבי's question about 37 does not fit with his own 'categories' answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction calls into question the whole 'categories' answer from step 5. The גמרא will need to explain how רב ביבי's two statements fit together.

phrases.aramaic: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: And Rav Beivai bar Abaye found it difficult:
"If so, that which we learned:
thirty-six כריתות in the Torah —
they are thirty-seven,
since there is 'one who offers up' and 'one who offers up'!"
phrases.notes: These are the two cases from the ruling just quoted: limbs from inside, and limbs from outside.

phrases.english: What is difficult for him?
Let him answer: he teaches the category of offering up!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ? נִישְׁנֵי: שֵׁם הַעֲלָאָה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction set up in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי's answer in step 5 that the משנה lists only categories.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His question 'it should be 37' only makes sense if the משנה counts each sin. Under his own 'categories' rule, one heading of 'offering up' would cover both cases.

steps.title: Shabbat and idol worship are different from offering up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב אחא: שבת and עבודה זרה have their details taught in their own places, so the כריתות list can mention just the category. העלאה has no such place, so רב ביבי's question was fair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these cases the same? The details of שבת and עבודה זרה are taught in their own places. So in the list of כריתות, which needs to mention them, he can answer that the משנה lists the category of שבת and the category of עבודה זרה. But for offering up, are the details taught in their own place, so that he could answer that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ביבי against רב אחא's challenge. The 'category' rule only works when the details are taught somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא said רב ביבי's own rule should have solved his question about 37. The answer is that the rule has a condition. A category is enough in our משנה only if the details are spelled out elsewhere, like the details of שבת and עבודה זרה. The ways of offering up outside are not spelled out anywhere else, so our משנה would have needed to count each one, and the question about 37 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? The two cases are not the same
In their own places, meaning in their own chapters elsewhere
Here: a general category or heading
Offering up a sacrifice, here outside the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves both of רב ביבי's statements from contradicting each other. It also shows that 'the משנה lists categories' is not a blanket rule.

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
Shabbat and idol worship:
the Tanna taught their details in their own places,
so in the list of karet cases, where they need to be mentioned,
he answers: 'It teaches the category of Shabbat,'
'it teaches the category of idol worship.'
But regarding offering up,
did the Tanna teach its details in their own place,
so that he could answer this way?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge in step 12 and defends רב ביבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a category is enough only when its details are taught elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ביבי's rule means the משנה always lists categories, so העלאה should count as one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only to topics like שבת and עבודה זרה, whose details appear elsewhere. העלאה does not qualify, so the question about 37 was valid.

steps.title: Two כריתות with only one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: if there are two punishments of כרת but only one לאו, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: two כריתות and one לאו, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. It is the reverse of an earlier rule about two לאוין with one כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא said that two לאוין with only one כרת still mean two separate חטאות. רבי ירמיה flips the case: two כריתות but only one לאו. Does that also bring two חטאות?

steps.title: The גזירה שוה gives slaughtering its own prohibition

steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that רבי עקיבא does not need a big action but does need a small one, and ידעוני has none at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש? Granted that רבי עקיבא does not need a big action, he does need a small action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how ריש לקיש keeps his reason even if the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש agrees that רבי עקיבא does not require a big action. But רבי עקיבא still requires some small action, and a ידעוני does nothing physical at all. So even by רבי עקיבא, ידעוני stays off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: granted that, even though
a big, significant action
a small, minor action

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons ידעוני is not on the כרת list: רבי יוחנן says it shares one לאו with אוב; ריש לקיש says it has no action at all, not even the small action that רבי עקיבא requires.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying רבי עקיבא requires no action at all. He is saying רבי עקיבא drops only the need for a BIG action; a small one is still needed.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish?

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא בָּעֵי מַעֲשֵׂה רַבָּה,
phrases.english: Granted that Rabbi Akiva does not require a significant action,
he does require a minor action.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ? נְהִי דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא בָּעֵי מַעֲשֵׂה רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends ריש לקיש against the challenge from רבי עקיבא in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of רבי עקיבא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא requires no action whatsoever.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא requires a minor action; ידעוני has none, so it is excluded.

steps.title: What action does a בעל אוב do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what small action a בעל אוב performs, since ריש לקיש said רבי עקיבא needs at least a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בעל אוב: what action is there in his sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests ריש לקיש's rule that רבי עקיבא needs at least a small action. It asks what that action is in the case of a בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש just said ידעוני has no action at all, so it cannot be in the list. But בעל אוב is in the list, so it must have some action. The גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A necromancer, someone who raises the spirits of the dead
A physical action

phrases.english: A necromancer,
what action is there in it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies ריש לקיש's 'small action' rule from Step 30 to the case of בעל אוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What counts as the small action in the sin of a בעל אוב?

steps.title: Striking his arms is the action
steps.stepSummary: The בעל אוב's striking of his arms counts as an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The striking of his arms counts as an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the בעל אוב strikes his arms together while doing his magic, and that counts as the action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'small action' ריש לקיש was talking about. It is enough for רבי עקיבא, who does not need a big action.

keyTerms.meaning: Striking or knocking his arms together

phrases.english: The striking of his arms is an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בעל אוב's action is striking his arms together.

steps.title: What action does a מגדף do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what action a blasphemer performs, since he only speaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blasphemer: what action is there in his sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about a מגדף, whose sin seems to be only speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a מגדף brings a חטאת. If רבי עקיבא needs at least a small action, the גמרא must find one in the מגדף's sin.

keyTerms.meaning: One who blasphemes, cursing ה׳'s name

phrases.english: A blasphemer, what action is there in it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְגַדֵּף, מַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as Step 31, now asked about the מגדף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What counts as the small action in the sin of a מגדף?

steps.title: Twisting his lips is the action
steps.stepSummary: The מגדף's twisting of his lips as he speaks counts as an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The twisting of his lips counts as an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that moving the lips to speak counts as the action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even speech involves a tiny physical motion of the lips. According to ריש לקיש, that is enough for רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Twisting or moving his lips

phrases.english: The twisting of his lips is an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מגדף's action is the twisting of his lips.

steps.title: Assumption: striking the arms counts even for the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes that striking the arms is a small action even according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We were thinking that striking the arms is a small action even according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what it first assumed: that striking the arms counts as a small action even for the רבנן, who do require an action. This line sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן argue with רבי עקיבא and require an action for a חטאת. The assumption is that striking the arms is enough even for them. The גמרא is about to show that this cannot fit ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It entered our mind; what we first assumed
A small action
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי עקיבא

phrases.english: It entered our mind:
the striking of his arms is a small action
even according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the answer of Step 32 into an assumption about the רבנן's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working assumption: striking the arms counts as a small action even for the רבנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא: עבודה זרה needs an action, including bowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying one is liable for עבודה זרה only for an act involving action, and it lists bowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: For עבודה זרה one is only liable for something with an action, such as slaughtering, burning incense, pouring wine, or bowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge to the assumption by quoting a ברייתא about עבודה זרה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires an action and then lists bowing as one of the actions. The next steps ask whether bowing really is an action.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
He bowed down

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
With idol worship one is not liable

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: except for a matter that has an action in it,
for example where he slaughtered, or burned incense,
or poured a libation, or bowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the assumption of Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that striking the arms is an action even for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a comparison to bowing. The full attack lands in Step 40.

steps.title: Bowing seems to have no action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an old difficulty: how can bowing count as an action?
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was hard for us: bowing has no action in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls a known difficulty with this ברייתא: bowing does not look like an action, so why is it listed? This sets up the earlier argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says only actions make you liable, yet it lists bowing. That looks like a contradiction inside the ברייתא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was difficult for us
Bowing down

phrases.english: And it was difficult for us:
bowing has no action in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַשְׁיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a known problem inside the ברייתא of Step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of bowing as an act with an action.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires an action, but bowing seems to have none.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answered that the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who does not require an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Whose view is this? It is רבי עקיבא's, who says an action is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls ריש לקיש's answer: the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, so bowing can be listed even though it is not a real action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying this, ריש לקיש shows that in his view bowing is not an action for the רבנן. Otherwise he would not need to say the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
We do not require an action

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Akiva's,
who says we do not require an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of Step 37 by assigning the ברייתא to רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bowing was listed as an action, and that seemed impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who does not require a real action.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: bending the body is an action, even for the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answered that the ברייתא can follow the רבנן, because bending one's body counts as an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it follows the רבנן, because bending his body counts as an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls רבי יוחנן's different answer: bowing does count as an action, because the person bends his whole body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן there is no problem with the ברייתא at all. Bending the body is a real action, even for the רבנן who require one.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
Bending his height; bending his body down

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
you can even say it is the Rabbis,
since the bending of his height is an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than ריש לקיש did in Step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what counts as an action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bowing seemed to have no action.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bending the body is an action, so the ברייתא can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: If bowing is not an action, how can striking the arms be one?
steps.stepSummary: From ריש לקיש's answer we learn that bending the body is not an action for the רבנן. Then how could striking the arms, a smaller motion, count for them?
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that ריש לקיש holds that, for the רבנן, bending the body is not an action. Would striking the arms then be an action?!
steps.whatsHappening: Here the challenge lands. The assumption from Step 35 cannot fit ריש לקיש's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bending the whole body is a bigger motion than striking the arms. If ריש לקיש holds that the bigger motion does not count for the רבנן, the smaller one surely does not count either.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; this shows that
According to the view of the Rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on ריש לקיש himself. It attacks only the גמרא's own assumption (Step 35) that striking the arms counts even for the רבנן.

phrases.english: By inference, Reish Lakish holds
according to the Rabbis

phrases.aramaic: כְּפִיפַת קוֹמָתוֹ לְרַבָּנַן לָא הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: that bending his height, for the Rabbis, is not an action.
Is the striking of his arms an action?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses ריש לקיש's answer in Step 38 to knock down the assumption of Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that striking the arms is an action even for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If bending the whole body is not an action for the רבנן, the smaller motion of striking the arms cannot be one either.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's 'small action' is only for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ריש לקיש meant striking the arms counts as a small action only according to רבי עקיבא, not according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when ריש לקיש said striking the arms is a small action, he meant according to רבי עקיבא. According to the רבנן it is not an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first assumption and limits ריש לקיש's statement to רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits ריש לקיש's whole approach. רבי עקיבא needs only a tiny action, and striking the arms is enough for him. The רבנן need a real action, and for them striking the arms is not one.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather; drop the earlier idea
According to the view of רבי עקיבא

steps.whatToRemember: For ריש לקיש there are three levels. The רבנן require a real action, and neither bowing nor striking the arms is enough for them. רבי עקיבא needs only a small action, such as striking the arms or twisting the lips. ידעוני has no action at all.

phrases.english: But rather, when Reish Lakish says
the striking of his arms is a small action,
it is according to Rabbi Akiva,
but according to the Rabbis it is not an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא כִּי קָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 40 by dropping the assumption of Step 35.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For ריש לקיש, striking the arms is a small action only according to רבי עקיבא. According to the רבנן it is not an action.

steps.title: Why does the משנה exclude only the blasphemer?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן hold that a בעל אוב does no action, the משנה should have excluded both the מגדף and the בעל אוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה say "Excluded is the blasphemer, since there is no action"? Let it say "Excluded are the blasphemer and the בעל אוב"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on the conclusion of step 41 and challenges the wording of the רבנן in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 41 said that, for the רבנן, the בעל אוב has no real action. The רבנן only bring a קרבן for sins with an action, and they excluded the מגדף for lacking one. So they should have excluded the בעל אוב too, but they did not.

keyTerms.meaning: One who blasphemes, cursing ה׳'s name
A necromancer, one who raises the dead to ask them questions
Literally 'went out'; here it means 'is excluded'
A physical action

phrases.english: If so,
why does it teach:
"Excluded is the blasphemer, since there is no action in it"?
phrases.notes: These are the words of the רבנן in our משנה.

phrases.english: Let it teach: "Excluded are the blasphemer and the necromancer"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 41 to attack the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the רבנן's exclusion in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the בעל אוב also has no action for the רבנן, he should have been excluded along with the מגדף.

steps.title: The משנה gave one of two examples
steps.stepSummary: The תנא mentioned only one of the two cases that have no action.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches one out of two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה did not need to list every case. It gave just one example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In fact, both the מגדף and the בעל אוב are excluded for the רבנן. The תנא simply mentioned one of them, and the other is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches one case out of two

phrases.english: It teaches one out of two.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 42
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial listing: the תנא gives one example to stand for both
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the בעל אוב means he is not excluded
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are excluded; only one was mentioned

steps.title: Then why not mention the בעל אוב instead?
steps.stepSummary: If only one example was needed, why choose the מגדף over the בעל אוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it teach the בעל אוב and not the מגדף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: if only one example was given, why was this one chosen?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא only needed one example of a sin with no action, either the מגדף or the בעל אוב would have done the job. So why did the רבנן pick the מגדף? The next step explains why the מגדף in particular had to be mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach

phrases.english: But let it teach the necromancer
and not teach the blasphemer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנֵי בַּעַל אוֹב וְלָא לִיתְנֵי מְגַדֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 43
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנא just picked one example
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only one example was needed, the תנא could just as well have named the בעל אוב. Choosing the מגדף needs a reason.

steps.title: The מגדף had to be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: Without mentioning the מגדף, we might think the רבנן agree to רבי עקיבא in his case, since his כרת appears in the section about קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מגדף had to be mentioned. You might have thought: since his כרת is written in the place of the קרבן, the רבנן agree with רבי עקיבא here. So it teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the מגדף is the case that needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the מגדף's כרת sits right in the section about the חטאת. That could make us think that here even the רבנן require a קרבן without an action. So the משנה names the מגדף to show that they do not. The בעל אוב had no such reason, so his exclusion is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
It could enter your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for certain sins
Agrees
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה names the מגדף because his case could have fooled us. The בעל אוב is also excluded for the רבנן, but he did not need to be named.

phrases.english: The blasphemer was necessary for him,
for it could enter your mind to say:
since his karet is written
in the place of an offering,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:27–30. The מגדף's כרת comes right after the חטאת passage.

phrases.english: say that they agree with Rabbi Akiva,
so it teaches us that they do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְגַדֵּף אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 44
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity: the chosen example was the one that needed teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of where his כרת is written, the רבנן would agree with רבי עקיבא about the מגדף
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן do not obligate the מגדף in a קרבן

steps.title: עולא: the בעל אוב burns incense to a demon
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the משנה's בעל אוב burns incense to a demon, which is a real action.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The בעל אוב that the משנה teaches is one who burns incense to a demon.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different answer to the question of step 42: the בעל אוב was not excluded because he really does an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying the משנה gave just one example, עולא changes what the בעל אוב case is. Burning incense is a full physical action. So even the רבנן agree he brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Burns incense
A demon

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The necromancer that the mishna teaches
is one who burns incense to a demon.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: בַּעַל אוֹב דְּקָתָנֵי בִּמְקַטֵּר לַשֵּׁד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 42
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so that it includes a real action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בעל אוב does no action for the רבנן and should have been excluded
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's בעל אוב burns incense, a real action, so he is not excluded

steps.title: רבא: that is just idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that burning incense to a demon is simply עבודה זרה, which the משנה already lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged it: If so, that is the same as one who worships עבודה זרה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering incense to a demon is worship. The משנה already lists עובד עבודה זרה, so the בעל אוב would be a repeat of a case already in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges, attacks a statement
That is the same as
One who worships idols

phrases.english: Rava challenges it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, הַיְינוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה!
phrases.english: If so, that is the same as one who worships idols!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, הַיְינוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects עולא's definition from step 46
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of the בעל אוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that definition the case repeats עבודה זרה, which is already listed.

steps.title: רבא: burning incense to gather demons
steps.stepSummary: רבא redefines the case: he burns incense not to worship the demon but to gather it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: One who burns incense to a demon in order to bind it together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps the idea of burning incense but gives it a different purpose, so that it is not worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is still a real action, so the רבנן's rule is kept. But the goal is magic, gathering the demons to use them, not worship. So it is a separate case from עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to, for the purpose of
To bind it together, to gather it

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
One who burns incense to a demon in order to bind it.
phrases.notes: He is not serving the demon. He is using the incense like a spell to gather demons together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes עולא's approach after רבא's own challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning incense to a demon must be worship
steps.terutzMaskana: It is incense burned as magic to gather demons, not as worship

steps.title: אביי: that is just a חובר חבר
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that gathering demons is the separate prohibition of חובר חבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, that is the same as a חובר חבר!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's new definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists חובר חבר, one who gathers or binds, as its own sin, separate from the בעל אוב. So רבא's case would be a different sin, not a בעל אוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A charmer, one who binds or gathers by magic

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so, that is the same as a charmer!
phrases.notes: דברים 18:11, where חובר חבר is listed separately from the בעל אוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִם כֵּן, הָיִינוּ חוֹבֵר חָבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's definition from step 48
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's definition of the בעל אוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gathering demons fits the separate category of חובר חבר, not בעל אוב.

steps.title: This kind of חובר חבר gets סקילה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a חובר חבר of this type, gathering demons, is punished with סקילה like a בעל אוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The תורה said that a חובר חבר like this one is punished with סקילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts that his case is a חובר חבר, but says this kind also counts as a בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny the overlap. A חובר חבר who gathers demons with incense falls under the severe law of the בעל אוב, which carries סקילה. So he can be the בעל אוב of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Such as this one
Death by stoning

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Torah said:
a charmer such as this is punished with stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה חוֹבֵר חָבֶר כְּגוֹן זֶה, בִּסְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 49
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the overlap but placing this case under the more severe category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every חובר חבר is a separate, lesser sin
steps.terutzMaskana: A חובר חבר who gathers demons like this is punished with סקילה, like a בעל אוב

steps.title: Then what is the ordinary חובר חבר?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: if this case gets סקילה, what case is the חובר חבר that is only a לאו?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the חובר חבר that is only a לאו, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי follows up on רבא's answer and asks him to identify the regular חובר חבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה also has a חובר חבר who breaks only a לאו, without סקילה. If gathering demons is the severe kind, אביי wants to know what the lighter kind is. This sets up the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment
Which one is it?

phrases.english: But then the charmer that is only a prohibition,
which one is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא חוֹבֵר חֶבֶר דִּבְלָאו – הֵדֵין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבא's answer in step 50 and sets up the next step
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is the חובר חבר that carries only a לאו

steps.title: The ordinary חובר חבר is someone who gathers animals by magic
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers אביי with a ברייתא: the חובר חבר that is only a לאו is someone who magically gathers animals, large or small, even snakes and scorpions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: As a ברייתא teaches about the פסוק "and a חובר חבר": this means both someone who gathers large animals and someone who gathers small animals. Even someone who gathers snakes and scorpions is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's question from Step 51. The ordinary חובר חבר, the one that is only a לאו, is someone who uses magic to gather animals together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had asked: if gathering demons gets סקילה, what case is left for the plain לאו of חובר חבר? רבא answers that the לאו covers gathering animals, not demons. This keeps both rules in place: gathering demons is like a בעל אוב and gets סקילה, while gathering animals is the basic לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא. This introduces a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה.
Someone who uses magic to gather creatures into one place. This is a prohibition from the תורה.
Someone who gathers large animals, or someone who gathers small animals.
Liable, meaning he has broken the prohibition.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of חובר חבר. Gathering demons gets סקילה, like a בעל אוב. Gathering animals, even small ones like snakes and scorpions, is the ordinary לאו.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חייב does not mean the death penalty. It means he is liable for breaking the לאו of חובר חבר. The death penalty of סקילה applies only to the demon case.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is taught:
phrases.notes: רבא is answering אביי's question from the last step.

phrases.english: "And a חובר חבר":
phrases.notes: דברים 18:11

phrases.english: both one who gathers large ones
and one who gathers small ones,
phrases.notes: He means large and small animals gathered by magic.

is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's question in Step 51 about which case the plain לאו of חובר חבר covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of חובר חבר is only a לאו, since gathering demons gets סקילה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gathering animals by magic, large or small, even snakes and scorpions.

steps.title: Gathering hornets and scorpions: forbidden, but allowed in self-defense
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that gathering a hornet and a scorpion by magic is forbidden, but it is permitted if they are chasing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone who wants to gather a hornet and a scorpion by magic is forbidden to do so. But if they are coming after him, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a practical rule to the ברייתא about gathering creatures. Doing it on purpose is forbidden, but doing it to protect yourself from creatures that are chasing you is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that even gathering snakes and scorpions is forbidden. אביי makes an exception: if the creatures are attacking, using the magic to stop them is permitted. The prohibition targets gathering them by choice, not defending yourself from danger.

keyTerms.meaning: To gather or bind together, here by magic.
A hornet and a scorpion.
Forbidden / permitted.
They are coming after him, meaning they are chasing him.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the prohibition of חובר חבר has an exception for danger. It is a practical rule about protecting yourself.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This one who wants
to gather a hornet and a scorpion,
phrases.notes: He means gathering them by magic, like the חובר חבר case just mentioned.

phrases.english: it is forbidden;
but if they are coming after him, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical self-defense exception to the ברייתא's rule about gathering snakes and scorpions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathering a hornet and a scorpion by magic is forbidden, but it is permitted if they are chasing him.

steps.title: Starting a challenge from רבי יוחנן's view that bending the body is an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge based on רבי יוחנן, who holds that bending one's body counts as an action. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוחנן, who says that bending one's body counts as an action, the twisting of...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It starts from רבי יוחנן's view that bending one's body counts as an action, and turns to the 'twisting' of the lips from Step 34. The challenge is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that, even for the רבנן, bending the body when bowing counts as an action (Step 39). The רבנן in our משנה exclude the מגדף because he does no action (Steps 42 and 45). The גמרא is about to ask how these fit together, since twisting the lips also seems to be a physical movement.

keyTerms.meaning: Bending one's body, literally "bending his height."
An action, a physical deed.
The twisting of. The sentence continues in the next section.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says
bending one's body is an action,
the twisting of...
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר כְּפִיפַת קוֹמָתוֹ הָוֵי מַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חובר חבר discussion and begins a new challenge about what counts as an action.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's statement in the משנה that the מגדף is excluded because he does no action (Steps 42 and 45), read according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If bending the body counts as an action even for the רבנן, then twisting the lips should arguably count too. In that case, why do the רבנן say the מגדף has no action? The rest of the challenge is on the next amud.
